scope: Frozen external-turn monitor API/package and isolated native tmux red-team QA. No source, test, or .gjc files were modified.

commands.name: exact isolated real-tmux external monitor test
commands.command: TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=server/tsconfig.json node --import tsx --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='real tmux external monitor notifies once per observed Codex turn and rebaselines restarts' server/modules/providers/tests/tmux-runtime.e2e.test.ts > artifacts/external-turn-tmux-e2e.tap

commands.name: runtime API/package red-team assertions
commands.command: TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=server/tsconfig.json node --import tsx --input-type=module <inline assertions for metadata validation, GJC exclusion, provider-ID conflict/privacy, semantic disarm, provider labels, and web-push channel-off>

contractCoverage.contract: Diagnostics and stats expose complete stable event counters for baseline, arm, notification, semantic disarm, prune, unavailable discovery/read, provider-ID conflict, and generation reset without native IDs, pane identity, transcript, PID, or start-time data.

A monitor silently baselines startup waiting, notifies exactly once for an observed running-to-waiting transition, suppresses duplicate waiting, and emits an opaque distinct ordinal completion key for a fast second turn.
Unavailable evidence preserves an arm; asking_user, unknown, and ended transcript evidence fail closed; only successful absence prunes and a rediscovered generation silently baselines.
Incomplete/invalid process metadata and unsupported/GJC sessions are excluded before resolve; positive finite fractional Linux start times remain valid process-generation evidence.
Late native ID binding is silent, omissions retain the binding, and a conflicting provider ID is neither resolved nor notified.
All five external provider parsers classify running, waiting, asking, and unknown evidence; unavailable resolver evidence fails closed.

API/package push behavior preserves provider labels, maps provider session IDs to app session IDs, deduplicates a completion key while allowing the next ordinal, and honors both liveStop preference-off and Web Push channel-off.
Actual isolated tmux discovery drives one-per-turn notification intent, prune, same-name process restart silent baseline, and distinct completion keys.

apiPackage.result: 20 focused API/package tests passed; diagnostics/stats, state-machine boundaries, generation metadata, and parser/resolver behavior are covered by the TAP artifact.
Provider session mapping, completion-key dedupe/next ordinal, liveStop preference, channel-off, and provider labels passed against an isolated database and mocked Web Push transport.

nativeTui.result: The exact named real-tmux E2E passed against an isolated tmux harness; it discovered a fake external Codex process and exercised completion, prune, same-name restart baseline, and key distinction.
